body.statement: Along each nonsaturated sequence with \(d\to\infty\) and \(d/[n\log(ed)]\to0\), does the normalized risk \((n\log(ed)/d)\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) converge to a finite positive limit, and can an estimator attaining that limit be derived through \(\mathscr H_\epsilon^{\mathrm{const}}\)?
body.proof_tex:
The matched frontier proves only
\[
 0<c_\epsilon\leq\liminf\frac{n\log(ed)}d\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}
 \leq\limsup\frac{n\log(ed)}d\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\leq C_\epsilon<\infty
\]
along every nonsaturated sequence in the question.  It neither proves equality of the liminf and limsup nor identifies a cone-dependent optimal leading constant or an attaining estimator.
body.justification: The matched rate makes a correctly normalized constant question well posed and asks whether the estimation upgrade can be sharpened from comparison constants to exact efficiency.
body.gap: CaiLow2011L1 obtains a Bernstein-constant characterization in a Gaussian absolute-value experiment, while JiaoHanWeissman2018L1 gives rate equivalence for multinomial distance; neither identifies the overlap-cone constant.
body.consumer: An exact constant would calibrate polynomial degree and quantify the efficiency price of unknown observational treatment imbalance.
